# Norland (01, engineer) — BAD-066

## Brief
Make the admin dashboard's `import 'server-only'` guard something a machine checks, so a future edit cannot drop it in silence.

## Why this ticket exists

BAD-052 split `admin/src/lib/accounts.ts` into `admin/src/lib/accounts/`. Thirteen leaves now carry `import 'server-only'` where one file did, and the split's own spike says to keep it on every leaf including the type-only ones. Nothing checks that claim. The proposer proved it: on the BAD-052 working tree they deleted line 1 (`import 'server-only';`) from `admin/src/lib/accounts/detail-types.ts` and re-ran the whole recipe — `npm run verify` in admin/ exit 0 (typecheck, eslint 0 errors, build compiled, check:standalone PASS, check:secrets PASS), the five text-assertion tests 28 pass / 0 fail, the export diff empty, `verify-moves` OK. Four checks, none noticed. `grep -rn server-only` over `test/`, `admin/scripts/` and `admin/eslint.config.mjs` returns nothing.

The guard matters because it is the only thing that makes a client component's *value* import of a server module fail loudly instead of shipping server code — or a secret — into the browser bundle.

## Objective

Add a check that fails when a module that ought to declare `import 'server-only'` does not. Land it where the repo's required checks already run.

## Where it goes

`test/server/admin-client-boundary.test.mjs`, as additional test(s) in that file. Read it first — it is the right home and most of the machinery is already there:

- it walks every `.ts`/`.tsx` under `admin/src`, reading sources with no build and no database (the reason the file exists: `admin/` is TypeScript and this repo's runner is `node --test` over plain JS);
- it already parses import statements, distinguishes `import type` from value imports, and resolves `@/x` and relative specifiers to files;
- it is run by the root `npm test`, which `.github/workflows/ci.yml:118` runs as a required check. An eslint rule in `admin/eslint.config.mjs` would only be seen by `admin-ci`'s `npm run verify`, and would cost a custom rule plugin. Prefer the test. If while working you conclude the lint rule is genuinely better, say so in your Result and file a proposal — do not switch without saying why.

Reuse that file's helpers rather than writing a second copy of `sources()` / `resolveSpec()`. Keep the existing two tests passing unchanged.

## The rule you must get right

A blanket "every `.ts` under `admin/src/lib/` carries it" is WRONG and would fail on today's tree. Verified against `origin/main`:

- Deliberately client-safe, no `server-only` and must stay that way: `lib/action-state.ts` (its head comment explains why it sits outside `lib/actions/`), `lib/cookies.ts`, `lib/env.ts`, `lib/format.ts`, `lib/platforms.ts`.
- `'use server'` leaves under `lib/actions/` — `accounts.ts`, `announcements.ts`, `collabs.ts`, `flags.ts`, `profiles.ts` — carry no `server-only` and must not: a server action is *meant* to be importable from a client component, where Next turns it into an RPC. (`lib/actions/auth-admin.ts` and `lib/actions/support.ts` do carry it; check what makes them different before you decide whether that is a rule or an accident, and say which in your Result.)
- The type-only leaves `lib/accounts/types.ts` and `lib/accounts/detail-types.ts` DO carry it and, per the spike, must. They import nothing at runtime — only `import type` — so a rule built on transitive value-imports alone will not catch a drop there. That is precisely the deletion the evidence used, so a rule that misses it fails this ticket.

Two shapes that between them cover the tree; use these, or something demonstrably better that satisfies the acceptance proof below:

1. **Transitive.** A module that value-imports (not `import type`) a module which declares `server-only` — or which imports a server-only package such as `next/headers` or `postgres` — must itself declare `server-only`. Exception: a `'use server'` module.
2. **Sibling.** Every module under a directory whose same-named barrel declares `server-only` (`lib/accounts.ts` over `lib/accounts/`, `lib/actions.ts` over `lib/actions/`) must declare it too. Exception: a `'use server'` module. This is what catches the type-only leaves.

Whatever you land, the failure message must name the offending file and say what to do, in the voice of the assertions already in that file.

## Done when

- `npm test` from the repository root is green on the unmodified tree, and your new test(s) actually ran (do not let them pass vacuously on an empty file list — assert the inventory is non-empty, the way a text-assertion test should).
- **The acceptance proof, run and pasted into your Result:** delete line 1 of `admin/src/lib/accounts/detail-types.ts`, run the suite, show it now FAILS with your message; restore the line, run again, show it passes. Do the same for a second case of your choosing that rule 1 covers (for example a new module under `admin/src/lib/` that value-imports `./db` without declaring `server-only` — write it, prove the failure, delete it).
- `cd admin && npm run verify` still exits 0 if you touched anything under `admin/` (you should not need to).
- The head comment of whatever you add explains the boundary and why `tsc`, `next build`, eslint and the existing checks cannot see it — the file's existing comments are the standard to match.

If a real module is missing the guard and should have it, that is a finding: put it in your Result and file a proposal, do not fix it silently under this ticket. (Adding the guard to a file that plainly should have had it is in scope only if you say so explicitly and prove it changes no behaviour.)
- Do not touch `test/server/functions.test.mjs` or anything needing a local Supabase stack; your tests must run with no database, no build, no network.
